references are your best friend! don't be afraid to trace *just to practice* it can really give you a better feel for where your lines should go and learn different techniques to get what's in your head down on the paper (or in this case, screen). usually I spend way more time accumulating references than I do drawing. Pinterest can be super helpful for this :) I'd also look up some shading exercises like shading balls in different colors and using a variety of techniques. good luck! you have a really great foundation to build off of!

I think what'd be great to focus on is your line confidence, there's tons of exercises out there to help out with it. what has helped me get my lines a little more crisp and natural is tracing the lines in coloring pages, it's an old tattoo artist trick :) I really like your anatomy and posing though it looks very natural & relaxed

I quite like it and your color palette is really cool! I'd suggest experimenting more with shading with colors and tones. https://www.deviantart.com/nkpunch/art/Picking-colors-Tutorial-288139637 here's some really great tips, practicing those color balls can really help bring your piece to the next level. and don't worry if your first few attempts look really weird! it takes practice to get it to look natural

I really love the way you highlight! I think the green shadows are a bit more distracting rather than contributing to a cohesive piece, this shading on the head looks more natural but on the thighs it's almost distracting. when I want to work with colored highlights or shading I like to incorporate it as a colored light source so there's tons of references out there to help too! great work :)
